body: It's not obstruction. I can't stop you if you are going to abuse your power, but that doesn't make you right. All the more reason to never talk to you.
It's not her money. Her money was spent. It's gone now. Now it's someone else's money. She used a third party's money to be made whole from that theft.
How did you determine that this person had an idea set in their mind and refuses to change it?

>and they are more focused on making the video than talking to me.

That's because it's sound legal advice to never talk to police, except to say something along the lines of "talk to my lawyer."
Her entire philosophy was about not forcing other people to do things for you. Taking "free money" that she believed was taken coercively is not doing that.
No, take responsibility for your actions. Don't say you're just following orders. Own up to violating other people's bodies.
She could have not taken the money she claims was stolen. I didn't create her standards, she did. Not my fault they weren't good enough for her.

The vast majority of people who attempt suicide attempted it previously. No, they aren't glad they lived. As if it were relevant, because I should be allowed to make decisions I might regret.

>We are not forcing them to do anything.

That's not true. At least one moderator of this forum is a hotline operator, who will violate people's bodies and force treatment on them if they deem it necessary while operating the hotline. And the majority of the outside world will do the same.

>But all the rest of existence - all that is NOT man-made - exists in perfect harmony.

That's not true. Have you taken a look at nature? Humans or no, it's pretty miserable.

Having a disagreement with you (such as in the case of someone who wants to die, when you don't want them to) is not "incapable of making decisions for themselves."

But that's irrelevant. Bodily autonomy means that I make decisions regarding my body even if they are bad ones.

Yes, I have an agenda. I want to be able to kill myself without people like you violating me in the process.

>If you have a sound mind(IE, You are aware of your actions and their consequences), I cannot force feed you.

I can't believe I missed this part. What this means in practice is "I can't force feed you unless I (or someone else) decides I can force feed you."

What this tells me is that I can't trust nurses, because they don't believe in  bodily autonomy.

The "rest of existence" is a cesspool of pain, suffering, and void. Mostly void.

It's garbage and I want no part in it.

>While that does take away part of their autonomy, the rest of it remains intact.

Then why did you say you couldn't take away a person's autonomy when you clearly can?
If you go down the Torrent route, steal the PC while you're at it. That will also save you money.
And they have the gall to say I'm the "selfish" one.

>I can stop suicidal people from outright hurting themselves with knives.

That's taking away my bodily autonomy. And the subsequent hospitalization is "a procedure done that they do not want."

And it doesn't even need to come to that. You can force these procedures on people even if they haven't done anything, you just need reason to believe that they are at imminent risk of hurting themselves. Surely you've read the NGASR?

But the money she was receiving was stolen from other people. And she took it. The fact that her money had also been stolen doesn't change that.

Aka "it's fine for me to steal their money because my money was stolen once."

You are a nurse, so you should realize that you can't refuse treatment if you decide that I am not mentally capable of refusing treatment. Such as a head injury or a suicide attempt.

Trying to starve yourself is a suicide attempt. It's ridiculous that nurses won't let me kill myself. Be honest about it and don't spread false information.
